title: Fomalhaut b: The First Planet We Ever Saw. Maybe.

target.note: v2: short declaratives, simple words, one idea per beat

narration:
Fomalhaut is the brightest star in the autumn sky. Easy to spot. Hard to forget.
Around it lies a ring. A wide, thin belt of dust and ice. It sits far past where any planet should be.
In 2008, something inside that ring caught the light and held it.
The first planet ever imaged in visible light around a star that was not our Sun.
That was the headline. The whole field sat back. That was supposed to be the end of the argument.
It was not the end. The signal is so faint that some astronomers still call it a dust cloud.
Just dust, kicked up by something invisible passing through the ring on its way out.
Or a real world, holding that whole belt in its gravity.
Same light. Same picture. Two very different things. No telescope alive can tell them apart.
Then there is the orbit. It swings in close to the star, then throws itself far out into the cold.
An orbit that wild does not stay tidy for long.
One bad pass. One nudge from that star. And it never comes back around.
So the likeliest ending is a long, silent fall out of the system. Nothing left out there to catch it.
The first planet we ever saw in visible light. Maybe a cloud. Maybe a world. Maybe already gone.
